thread:
maria: Quick proposal check — I want to carry a small QoS tag through the request path and have the routing adjudicator blend it into route scoring at admission time. Goal: let latency-sensitive requests bias towards low-latency routes without changing long-term policy artifacts (no persistent changes to cache keys or policy graphs). Thoughts?

alex: Sounds useful. couple questions: is QoS only an admission bias or does it persist into tracing/telemetry? and how do we avoid gaming? :thinking_face:

maria: Plan is ephemeral: QoS travels as request metadata (e.g. header X-Redwood-QoS: urgent|standard|background). It gets applied to scoring with a configurable alpha so we can fade its effect. We explicitly DO NOT change route compatibility or global caches.

jon: 👍 on ephemeral. important: KV/prefix caches and batching must remain deterministic. if QoS causes different model variant choices, cache semantics could diverge. we should forbid QoS from altering cache keys.

sasha: Ops/availability question — if QoS prefers a low-latency region but that region is at capacity, do we preempt other tenants or fallback to higher-latency region? need clear preemption policy and observability for swapped routes.

maria: Proposal: QoS only influences score; the admission decision still respects capacity tiers and SLA fallback rules. i.e. we bias towards preferred routes but never violate hard capacity constraints. if we fall back, annotate the request with the reason.

alex: Implementation notes: add a new ScoreInput field: qos_multiplier (float), default 1.0. final_score = base_score * (1 + alpha * (qos_multiplier - 1)). keep alpha per-tenant and global tunable.

jon: Also add unit test for sequence-length-aware choices. QoS should not override short-seq fast-paths (we have fast kernel lanes that are sequence-length tuned). add integration test with simulated load showing no cache churn.

ops-bot: test-runner: spike branch 'qos-adjudicator-spike' -> unit tests passed (23/23), integration smoke failed 1/8: observed cache key drift on batching simulator.

maria: Good catch from ops-bot. Fix: ensure QoS is stripped before cache key generation in batching layer. keep it in request meta only for scoring.

alex: API contract to document: header name, allowed values, semantics (ephemeral), alpha default, telemetry fields (routing.qos.requested, routing.qos.applied, routing.qos.fallback_reason).

jon: Runtime interface change: minimal shim in scorer interface so existing adapters get qos in ScoreInput but adapters must ignore it if they can't respect it. add a compatibility flag 'supports_qos_hint' to adapter registration.

sasha: Rollout plan: 1) spike & unit tests (this week), 2) canary in dedicated west-2 with alpha=0.2, telemetry enabled (next week), 3) broader canary + ops runbook adjustments, 4) GA toggle off by default for legacy tenants.

maria: Action items: alex owns API docs + header, jon owns scorer shim + tests, sasha owns rollout + runbook, i'll open the RFC PR. tagging eng-qa for canary scenarios.

eng-qa: will prepare canary test matrix: latency-sensitive mix (10%), regular (80%), background (10%), region-failure scenario. will validate no cache divergence and trace annotation correctness.

maria: Thanks — I'll open the draft PR and link here. if anyone objects to the ephemeral approach speak now, otherwise i'll proceed with spike. :thumbsup:
